claims.text: The FeNiCrMn alloy is obtained by removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The target FeNiCrMn alloy is in a solidified solid-solution state.
Removing Co alters lattice distortion in FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co alters local magnetic interactions in FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The lattice-distortion and magnetic changes caused by Co removal influence dislocation-core structures.
The absence of Co increases lattice distortion.
The lattice-distortion and magnetic changes caused by Co removal lower the effective energy barrier for dislocation motion.
Dislocation glide and associated restoration processes can be thermally activated in high-entropy alloys.
A lower dislocation-motion barrier in the Co-free alloy produces a lower activation volume.
A lower dislocation-motion barrier in the Co-free alloy produces higher strain-rate sensitivity.
The Co-free alloy will have a statistically lower activation volume than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under matched testing conditions.
The Co-free alloy will have a greater flow-stress sensitivity to strain rate than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under matched testing conditions.
The proposed activation behavior underpins a favorable strength-ductility balance across a wide temperature range.
Strain rate can affect strength, dislocation activation, and dislocation density during high-rate deformation of CoCrFeMnNi and a related Mn-free alloy.
The relative contributions of twinning and dislocation-mediated deformation can vary with temperature.
The proposed comparison is bounded to approximately 77-900 K and strain rates from about 10^-3 s^-1 to dynamic rates above 10^3 s^-1.
The controlled comparison uses Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi specimens with identical processing histories and comparable microstructures.
Activation volume can be obtained from the proposed stress-relaxation and strain-rate-sensitivity analyses.
